stem: What is the practical benefit of building a circuit from named registers such as `QuantumRegister(3, 'data')` and `QuantumRegister(1, 'anc')` instead of the bare `QuantumCircuit(4)` form?

options.text: Named registers usually make the circuit execute faster on hardware.
They let you address qubits by role, e.g. `data[0]` and `anc[0]`, which keeps larger circuits readable.
Only qubits that belong to a named register can be measured; anonymous qubits cannot.
Named registers are required by the transpiler, which refuses a circuit built with the bare `QuantumCircuit(4)` form.
Named registers usually let the transpiler keep the `data` qubits contiguous on the device, which improves the layout.
Named registers typically survive transpilation, so the ISA circuit still shows `data` and `anc` labels instead of `q`.

explanation.correct: Registers are an organizational tool. Naming them lets you reference qubits/bits by role (`data`, `anc`) and index within each group, which keeps larger circuits readable and lets one circuit contain multiple distinct registers. They carry no performance or execution requirement.

distractors.A: Register naming is purely structural metadata; it has no effect on execution speed.
distractors.C: Any qubit can be measured regardless of whether it lives in a user-named register; `QuantumCircuit(4)` qubits are measurable too.
distractors.D: Circuits built with the integer form transpile perfectly well; the transpiler never inspects register names.
distractors.E: The layout pass optimizes on connectivity and error rates; it never reads register names, so grouping by register buys no locality.
distractors.F: A transpiled circuit is defined over the device's physical qubits and carries a single register named `q`; your names live on in the layout, not in the ISA circuit's registers.

provenance.notes: high length tell + absolute-wording tell cleared (correct trimmed, distractor D given substance, distractor A now hedges) | pool wave: +E (register names believed to steer the layout) +F (register names believed to survive transpilation)
